title: Female borrowers who describe transitioning to a new business venture may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention the number of children may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention specific institutional affiliations or training programs may fund more slowly.
Male borrowers who include specific details about family members, such as ages or spouse's job, may fund faster.
Female borrowers who describe participation in specific microfinance programs like BRAC may fund faster.
Female borrowers who specify the number of children currently in school may fund faster.
Female borrowers who identify as single or separated mothers may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention creating employment or earning opportunities for young people may fund faster.
Female borrowers who include specific details about their educational background may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who include loan amounts in local currency fund more slowly.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who use aspirational language such as 'dreams' for their business fund faster.
Mentioning a history of previous loan repayment predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Providing specific operational or inventory details predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Specifying the number of years a business or trade has been operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize family and household details fund more slowly.
